<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type

| Field | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | **CONFIRMED** — workflow label projection is incomplete across direct phase checkpoints |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium — durable state and comments advance, while the issue projection can remain stale |
| Task Type | Bug fix with regression coverage |

### What Was Claimed

Issue `#92` reports that picked-up issues advance through durable ForgeDock phases and comments while their visible `workflow:*` label remains at an earlier phase. The expected projection is one canonical current workflow label, with unrelated labels preserved, throughout investigation, build, review, merge, and terminal states.

### What We Found

- `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel` already performs a read/replace/write projection: it removes existing `workflow:*` labels, adds the requested canonical label, and preserves ordinary labels such as `bug` and priority labels.
- Direct child checkpoints call `setWorkflowLabel` through `workflowLabelForCheckpoint`, but that mapping emits labels only for phase starts and investigation completion. Plan, worktree preparation, implementation, verification, review completion, and merge checkpoint transitions are not fully represented.
- Complete phase projection currently renders the phase report before attempting the label update. A report projection failure therefore leaves the durable phase event recorded without attempting the corresponding label projection on that invocation.
- The parent node path has a broader transition mapper, but direct work-on runs use the checkpoint path. Direct finalization records merge start before merging yet does not project `workflow:awaiting-merge` at the merge boundary.
- Existing tests cover a single label replacement and isolated node-stage mappings, but do not exercise the complete checkpoint lifecycle or assert that every transition removes the previous workflow label while retaining unrelated labels.

### Root Cause

Workflow-state label derivation is split between the parent node mapper and a partial child checkpoint mapper. The child mapper has no complete-phase mapping for most phases and no merge-stage mapping, so a successful durable checkpoint can leave the prior workflow label untouched. The projection ordering further couples label reconciliation to report rendering.

### Affected Files

- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` — checkpoint label derivation and side-effect ordering.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — direct merge-boundary label projection.
- `src/adapters/github-projection.ts` — existing replacement/preservation contract to retain and test.
- `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts` and `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` — lifecycle regression coverage.

### Evidence

1. `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` in `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` maps `start` for only investigation/build/review and maps `complete` only for investigation.
2. `forge_checkpoint` appends the phase event, renders complete reports, then invokes the derived label projection; missing mappings produce no label write.
3. `setWorkflowLabel` filters `label.startsWith("workflow:")` before PUT, demonstrating the intended single-current-workflow-label contract.
4. `workflowStageForNodeTransition` in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` already defines canonical stage transitions for parent nodes, including `awaitingMerge` and `merged`, showing the expected lifecycle vocabulary.

### History Findings

The supplied repository context and current source show an existing partial workflow-label implementation and focused unit tests, but no historical artifact was supplied that explains or completes the child checkpoint mapping. The fix should preserve the existing canonical label constants and idempotent replacement behavior rather than introduce a second label vocabulary.

### Recommendation

Centralize checkpoint stage derivation on the canonical `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE` values, project labels for every applicable phase start and completion (including merge start/completion), perform label reconciliation independently of report rendering, and add lifecycle tests that assert stale workflow labels are removed while unrelated labels survive each transition.

### Related Issues

None identified in the supplied issue and repository context.

### Decomposition Assessment

The change is bounded to deterministic projection and tests. It does not require decomposition, API redesign, UX changes, or security-authority decisions.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Each applicable phase start and completion projects the canonical current workflow label.
- [ ] The previous `workflow:*` label is removed on every transition.
- [ ] Non-workflow labels remain unchanged.
- [ ] Investigation, build, review, awaiting-merge, and merged lifecycle transitions have automated coverage.
- [ ] Required `check` verification remains green.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Allowed Paths

| Path | Allowed Changes |
| --- | --- |
| `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` | Derive checkpoint labels from canonical workflow stages; cover applicable phase starts/completions; make label reconciliation independent of complete-report rendering; export the pure mapper for tests. |
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Project `workflow:awaiting-merge` at the direct merge actuation boundary and preserve cancellation propagation for workflow-label writes. |
| `test/agents/child-runtime-commit.test.ts` | Add pure checkpoint-lifecycle mapping regression coverage. |
| `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts` | Extend fake GitHub projection coverage across the canonical lifecycle, asserting stale workflow-label removal and unrelated-label preservation. |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Extend canonical transition expectations where needed for the direct merge boundary. |

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change issue scope, workflow state authority, lease/CAS semantics, branch or merge policy, review authority, or GitHub API authentication.
- Do not add a second workflow-label vocabulary or alter unrelated artifact marker formats.
- Do not remove the required read-back/retry behavior of GitHub projections.
- Do not modify `.forge/config.json`, protected-branch policy, package dependencies, or generated runtime artifacts.
- Do not broaden label mutation to arbitrary issue labels; only the current canonical `workflow:*` label may be replaced.
- Do not use raw shell, direct GitHub writes, or paths outside the assigned worktree.

### Invariants

- At most one canonical `workflow:*` label remains after a successful workflow projection.
- Existing non-workflow labels remain in the issue label set.
- Durable checkpoint events remain authoritative; projection failures remain retryable and do not fabricate state transitions.
- Canonical labels continue to come from `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE`.
- Existing parent-node transition behavior remains unchanged except for signal propagation and the explicitly bounded direct merge projection.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Issue Criterion | Implementation Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Correct label at phase starts/completions | Complete pure phase/action mapping in `child-runtime.ts`; direct merge boundary maps to `awaitingMerge`. |
| Previous workflow label removed | Existing `setWorkflowLabel` replacement path exercised for every lifecycle transition. |
| Non-workflow labels preserved | Lifecycle adapter test retains `bug` and priority labels after each replacement. |
| Automated lifecycle coverage | Mapping and adapter tests cover investigation, ready-to-build, building, review, awaiting-merge, and merged states. |

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### Repository and CI Surface

- TypeScript ESM package; required verification command is `npm run check` through the named `check` Forge command.
- Canonical workflow labels are declared in `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts`.
- Direct work-on checkpoint side effects are implemented in `src/agents/child-runtime.ts`.
- Parent orchestration and direct finalization are implemented in `src/workflows/work-on.ts`.
- Projection tests use deterministic fake GitHub transports and do not require credentials or production issue data.

### Relevant Symbols

- `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel`
- `workflowLabelForCheckpoint`
- `workflowStageForNodeTransition`
- `WorkOnWorkflow.#projectWorkflowStage`
- direct finalization merge gate before `github.mergePullRequest`

### Hazards and Failure Modes

- A mapping that updates only starts can leave a prior label after a terminal or resumed completion.
- A mapping that treats review completion as merge readiness would misrepresent pending CI/merge authority; review remains `workflow:in-review` until the merge gate is authorized.
- Report projection and label projection must be independently retryable.
- Tests must distinguish `workflow:*` labels from unrelated labels and avoid asserting request ordering that is not part of the contract.

### Compatibility

The public GitHub adapter contract and artifact marker formats remain unchanged. Exporting a pure mapper is additive and exists to make the deterministic lifecycle contract directly testable.
<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Architecture Plan

1. Import `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE` into the child runtime and define a pure checkpoint stage mapper covering resolve/investigate, build phases, review, and merge for both starts and completions. Use the investigation verdict only for invalid routing; otherwise retain the correct active lifecycle stage.
2. Have the checkpoint tool reconcile the derived label before complete-phase report/artifact projection so a report-side failure cannot suppress the label attempt. Keep queue actions free of external projection.
3. Pass the extension signal through `#projectWorkflowStage` and project `awaitingMerge` immediately before the direct finalization merge call after all review/CI/authority gates pass.
4. Add focused tests for the pure mapper and expand adapter lifecycle tests to transition through canonical labels while preserving unrelated labels and removing all stale workflow labels.
5. Run the required named `check` command, inspect the final bounded diff, create the implementation commit, prepare the PR, and conduct the required fresh correctness/security review panel.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every applicable direct checkpoint start/completion yields the canonical current label.
- [ ] Investigation completion routes to `ready-to-build`, `invalid`, or `decomposed` only when its typed verdict warrants it.
- [ ] Review remains `in-review` until merge authority; merge start is `awaiting-merge`, merge completion is `merged`.
- [ ] Stale `workflow:*` labels are removed and unrelated labels survive each projection.
- [ ] Required `check` passes.

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
